goal:
A reviewer asked me to double-check a value from the 2024 paper by Nakamura and colleagues on phoneme drift in Journal of Cold-Region Materials (http://journal-of-cold-region-materials.example/articles/b49604-a-stochastic-model-of-phoneme-drift).
What estimated capacity does Table 2 report for station B-04? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

paragraphs: We study phoneme drift across five monitoring stations using a mixed-effects model.
Authors: Bilal Nakamura, Uri Abernathy. Published in Journal of Cold-Region Materials, 2024.
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report estimated capacity measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2022 and 2024. A pilot survey in 2019 had put the regional estimated capacity at 3.3 bits/param; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of phoneme drift relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2021 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2024 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the estimated capacity for each station in the 2024 campaign. The largest change relative to 2021 was observed at station L-08.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Ekstrom et al. (2018). [2] Wenzel and Castell (2020). [3] Quiroga et al. (2021).
